title: 7-round AES-128: precomputed collision key search

target.description: AES-128 on 128-bit blocks, reduced to 7 rounds. The collision is between internal byte-valued functions under the same unknown round keys, not between two AES master keys. Enumerate complete AES-128 keys and use a precomputed collision pair for the key-dependent twelve-byte parameter to screen each candidate, followed by plaintext/ciphertext verification.

setting.key_relation: One unknown standard AES master key; no related-key or known-key access.
setting.key_population: general keys, with a fixed precomputed table covering only an estimated half of parameter/key values; uncovered keys cause failure
setting.plaintext_model: Acquire the same 2^32 four-varying-byte plaintext structure as in the preceding attack.
assumptions: The source describes right-going ShiftRow. Standard AES uses left-going shifts. Reindexing columns by J(r,c)=(r,-c mod 4) conjugates the independent-round-key construction; inputs, outputs and recovered round keys are reflected consistently before standard key expansion. This coordinate normalization is a local structural interpretation, not a complete attack reproduction.
The four c-dependent internal constants are modeled heuristically as a random 32-bit function of the chosen three-byte c value; collision probabilities use this model.

The key-dependent twelve-byte parameter determines which collision-table entry is used. Empty entries exclude a subset of keys; the source does not claim fresh independent one-half success on every repeated run with the same table.

time.reported: Marginally less than exhaustive enumeration of 2^128 keys
time.note: The source claims slightly less than one reference Rijndael encryption per tested key, without a quantified factor. No invented 127.x exponent is assigned, and reusable preprocessing is separate.

data.note: All four-byte plaintext choices are acquired before filtering candidate keys.

memory.reported: Table indexed by 256^12 = 2^96 parameter values, holding a c-pair or an empty entry
memory.note: Each stored pair contains two three-byte c values. Representation, empty-entry flags, search working memory and whole-procedure peak are not priced, so no numeric peak in bits or bytes is inserted.

preprocessing.note: For each of 256^12 parameter values the source searches about 256^2 c values for a collision. The exponent is the product of these explicit counts, excluding unpriced sorting/indexing overhead.

success.description: The source allows failure for an estimated half of key/parameter values whose table entry has no collision. The recorded one-half is approximate key-population coverage, not repeated independent success for a designated uncovered key.

evidence.interpretation: Primary-source endpoint preserving the stated target, access model, native resource units and recovery scope. Paper-local pagination is distinct from the whole-proceedings PDF page number.

evidence.locator: CompletechapterPDF230–241 in original AES3volume; chapter1–12, allSections1–5 and references.
evidence.interpretation: Complete exact-edition contribution inventory checked; finite component controls and full attack/proof reproduction remain separate.

limitations: Costs and success statements are the authors' analytical claims; no complete attack or third-party implementation was executed.
